warnings.title: The B1 fix's ODN-10 justification is false as written: balance.json's top-level loader uses jint (silent decimal truncation), not jint_strict — a fractional cap value would NOT fail-fast
warnings.evidence: spec: 'balance.json loads with parse_integers = true + jint_strict, core/catalog.odin:675 — a fractional cap would fail-fast at catalog load' · catalog.odin:675 'v, e := json.parse(src.balance, parse_integers = true)' · catalog.odin:680 'b.logic_hz = jint(obj, "logic_hz", 0)' (all top-level balance keys use jint) · catalog.odin:1026-1033 jint: 'case json.Float: return i32(x)' (silent truncation) · jint_strict comment at :1036: 'the 3.1 integer-only bar for the NEW catalogs (ODN-5; the old loaders keep jint)' — jint_strict call sites are only node_types/pipe_tiers/packet_types/surges/demand/placement (:355-:624, :794-795)
warnings.detail: The canon asserts a fail-fast that does not exist for a top-level balance key: a minion copying the neighboring jint pattern gets 0.5→0 (accrue 0, eligible set permanently empty, spawns silently dead) — the exact silent failure the canon claims is impossible. The specified int form itself is compliant and safe.
warnings.recommended_fix: Pin the accessor in card 5.9: load cap_fraction_permille with jint_strict (the placement precedent, catalog.odin:794) + a 1..1000 range check; correct the 'loads with jint_strict' claim on the five surfaces.
